title: FDA NTI, fully replicate, CVwT 25% against CVwR 10%, ratio 0.975, n=32

oracle.arguments: power.NTID(CV=c(0.25, 0.10), theta0=0.975, n=32, design="2x2x4", details=TRUE, nsims=1e5)
oracle.method_note: PowerTOST computes empirical power by simulating nsims studies from the distributional properties of the deciding statistics. be-stats analyses datasets, so the Python side simulates studies and applies the be-stats criterion to each. Two Monte Carlo estimates of one probability, compared at the only layer both expose.

comparisons.tolerance_basis: DERIVED, and independent of the answer. Both sides estimate the same probability by simulation, so the difference between them has standard deviation sqrt(p(1-p)(1/n_python + 1/n_R)). Evaluated at the WORST CASE p = 0.5, which maximises p(1-p), and taken at four standard deviations: 4 * sqrt(0.25 * (1/20000 + 1/100000)) = 0.01549. Using worst-case p rather than the observed p means the tolerance was fixed before either side was run. Wide enough that two agreeing implementations pass essentially always; narrow enough that a procedural difference of more than about 1.5 percentage points fails.

not_cross_checkable: The overall p(BE). It requires criterion (b), the unscaled 80.00-125.00% test, which for a fully replicate study is FDA Appendix C's mixed model and is not implemented.
p(BE-ABE), PowerTOST's conventional ABE component. That is the same missing criterion (b) seen from the other side - PowerTOST computes it, be-stats cannot, so the comparison has one operand.
The Howe intermediates, for the same reason as the RSABE cases.
notes: The test product is markedly less reproducible than the reference. This is the axis criterion (c) exists to police, and the one a central case cannot exercise at all. Note PowerTOST takes CV as c(CVwT, CVwR) in that order.
